entry.title: CFTC Sues Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $397M DeFi Ponzi
entry.summary: The CFTC filed a lawsuit against Goliath Ventures, alleging a $397 million DeFi liquidity pool Ponzi scheme. The complaint allocates $87 million to Ponzi payments, $174 million to recruiter commissions, and $48 million to CEO Christopher Delgado's personal spending. This is one of the largest CFTC enforcement actions against a DeFi-related fraud, underscoring that regulators view DeFi platforms as subject to anti-fraud enforcement. It also highlights risks for retail investors in unaudited liquidity-pool schemes and may accelerate regulatory scrutiny of DeFi market structure. According to the complaint, roughly 1,600 customers are seeking recoveries through a bankruptcy estate. The scheme allegedly diverted funds to recruiter commissions and Ponzi payouts rather than generating legitimate returns from liquidity provision.

entry.title: SEC Prepares Escape Hatch From Securities Registration for Crypto Projects
entry.summary: The SEC has scheduled an open meeting for August 14 to consider proposing 'Regulation Crypto,' a tailored framework that would allow digital-asset projects to raise capital without full securities registration and provide an exit from SEC oversight once projects decentralize. This would mark the SEC's first durable rule for the crypto industry, offering founders a regulatory runway to raise capital and decentralize without triggering registration. It could reshape how U.S. crypto projects structure fundraising and reduce the threat of enforcement when legislation like the Clarity Act stalls. The proposal, advanced by SEC Chair Paul Atkins, is expected to include a startup exemption that could last up to four years and a safe harbor tied to decentralization, though fundraising thresholds were not disclosed. It would be the first formal rulemaking rather than a staff statement, making it harder for a future chair to unwind, and it comes after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act before its August recess.

entry.title: Bybit Secures US Asset Freeze in $1.5B Lazarus Hack Lawsuit
entry.summary: Bybit filed a civil lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia against North Korea, its Reconnaissance General Bureau, and the Lazarus Group over the $1.5 billion theft in February 2025, and secured a preliminary injunction freezing identified stolen assets. The court found Bybit likely to succeed on the merits. This is a major legal escalation in the largest crypto exchange hack, potentially setting a precedent for how exchanges can use civil courts and asset freezes to pursue state-sponsored hackers. It also demonstrates growing cooperation between the crypto industry, regulators, and law enforcement in tracing and recapturing stolen funds. Bybit reported that approximately $48.4 million has been recovered and about $30.5 million frozen across more than 28 exchanges and custodians, totaling roughly 5% of the stolen amount. The attackers drained about 500,000 ETH by manipulating a signing interface, and most of the stolen Ethereum was converted to Bitcoin via Thorchain and mixed through Wasabi, Tornado Cash, and Railgun.

entry.title: US Sanctions Expose $6.3B Iran-Russia Crypto Pipeline via Shelbit, Aban Tether
entry.summary: On August 7, the US Treasury sanctioned Iranian-linked crypto platforms Shelbit and Aban Tether, and TRM Labs traced over $6.3 billion through Shelbit-linked wallets over 23 months, including $318 million tied to Russia's sanctioned A7 network. The sanctions also targeted Shelbit founder Siavash Kayvanpour and several of his companies. This action reveals a large-scale crypto settlement pipeline used by sanctioned Iranian and Russian entities, highlighting how stablecoins like USDT on Tron have become a channel for evading international financial controls. It is likely to intensify regulatory scrutiny and compliance requirements on crypto exchanges and stablecoin issuers worldwide. Shelbit operated as a settlement network rather than a true exchange: its high-volume wallets' inflows and outflows matched within 0.1%, and it rotated addresses every one to four months. About 88% of the traced volume moved over Tron via USDT-TRC20, while only roughly $370,000 involved mixing services.

entry.title: World Liberty Took $100M From Businessman in Money Laundering Probe
entry.summary: According to NYT via The Block, World Liberty Financial received $100 million from businessman Guren "Bobby" Zhou, who is under an active money laundering investigation by British officials as of late July. No charges have been filed against Zhou. This news adds to mounting concerns about World Liberty Financial's ties to individuals under legal scrutiny, potentially affecting its regulatory standing and public perception. It also underscores the broader debate over crypto projects accepting funds from politically sensitive sources. The investor, Guren "Bobby" Zhou, has not been charged, but British officials told the Times that the investigation remained active as of late July. World Liberty is a DeFi protocol launched in 2024 with ties to the Trump family, which receives 75% of net proceeds from token sales.
